decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add/edit/delete bookmarks — URL…” Round 1 client did not contest URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The proposed specification includes saving bookmarks by URL; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add/edit/delete bookmarks — URL, title, description…” and metadata is fetched “when you paste a URL.” Round 1 client asks to keep automatic details with manual fallback.
decisions.note: Editable title and description are presented alongside pre-save metadata collection; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add/edit/delete bookmarks.” Round 1 client does not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion is included; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits automatic collection to “page title & favicon”; the reference also requires description and preview image. Round 1 client says “keep automatic page details with a manual fallback” without identifying the omitted fields.
decisions.note: The initial metadata decision is narrower than the reference, and the response does not expressly surface that difference; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Organize with tags.” Round 1 client retains tags as part of the expected search and organization behavior.
decisions.note: Tag assignment/organization is included; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes search across “title/description/tags,” omitting URL and notes. Round 1 client specifies “Search across URL, title, description, and notes.”
decisions.note: The client replaces the narrower field scope with the reference-conforming full-text fields; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents tags as another full-text field: “search across title/description/tags,” rather than presenting the required `#tag` syntax. Round 1 client says search should include tags but does not identify the syntax difference.
decisions.note: The required tag-token interaction is absent from the presented search language and is not expressly surfaced; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Filter by tag.” Round 1 client does not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Selecting a tag to filter bookmarks is included; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's editable fields omit notes but offers “notes” as a possible missing feature. Round 1 client selects it explicitly: “Notes on bookmarks, with simple Markdown formatting.”
decisions.note: The client selects the offered reference-conforming notes capability, including editable Markdown content; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export (browser bookmarks HTML)” as a possible addition rather than part of the proposed default. Round 1 client explicitly expects “Import … of browser bookmark HTML files.”
decisions.note: The client selects inclusion of the offered import capability; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export (browser bookmarks HTML)” as a possible addition rather than part of the proposed default. Round 1 client explicitly expects “… export of browser bookmark HTML files.”
decisions.note: The client selects inclusion of the offered export capability; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no read-later state. Round 1 client adds “Read-later status.”
decisions.note: The client supplies a related missing core requirement; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no unread perspective. Round 1 client adds “a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing unread-list requirement; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no archive state. Round 1 client adds “Reversible archiving.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing reversible archive behavior; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes deletion but no distinct archive semantics. Round 1 client specifies archiving must be “separate from permanent deletion.”
decisions.note: The client expressly adds the reference distinction between reversible archive and permanent delete; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default does not address duplicate URLs. Round 1 client requires duplicates “to open the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating another.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing duplicate-convergence rule; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only proposes ordinary full-text search. Round 1 client adds “AND/OR/NOT combinations.”
decisions.note: The client surfaces the missing Boolean-search requirement, although the response does not spell out every edge rule; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only proposes ordinary full-text search. Round 1 client adds “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing exact-phrase behavior; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no sorting. Round 1 client adds “Sorting.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing sorting capability; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no multi-selection or bulk actions. Round 1 client adds “bulk actions.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing bulk-action capability; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no collection-wide filtered action. Round 1 client explicitly requires “actions on everything matching the current filter.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing current-filter scope rule; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no reusable filter. Round 1 client adds “Saved searches/filters.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing saved-filter capability; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no page preservation. Round 1 client adds “A saved local copy of the page, including PDFs.”
decisions.note: The client adds local snapshots and explicitly surfaces the PDF case; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no Internet Archive action. Round 1 client adds “an option to save it to the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing Internet Archive capability; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 proposed default contains no profile display settings. Round 1 client adds “default sorting, number shown, and text size.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing display-preference requirements; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Add / edit / delete,” with bookmark details and notes covered elsewhere in the same presentation. Round 2 client says “This covers what I wanted” and accepts.
decisions.note: The implemented CRUD presentation conforms to the recorded reference behavior; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says metadata collection pulls “title/description/favicon,” still omitting the required preview image. Round 2 client gives only general approval: “This covers what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised metadata presentation fixes description but remains narrower than the reference; bare approval does not establish awareness; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Read-later status” with an unread indicator. Round 2 client accepts the application.
decisions.note: Read-later state is presented as implemented; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents a “dedicated Unread view.” Round 2 client accepts the application.
decisions.note: A separate unread list conforms to the reference; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists “bulk read” among available actions, allowing a selected bookmark to be marked read and removed from the unread state. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: The presented action provides the required transition to read; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents reversible “archive/unarchive” and a “Separate Archived view.” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Reversible archiving and a separate archive perspective conform; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says archive/unarchive “is distinct from permanent delete,” and permanent deletion confirms first. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Archive and delete are expressly distinguished; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents Markdown notes with “Write/Preview tabs” and rendered formatting. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Writing and rendering Markdown notes conforms; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: an existing URL “opens the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating a copy.” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Duplicate saves converge to editing the existing item; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents search “Across URL/title/description/notes/tags.” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: The required full-text fields are present; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents tag search through the field prefix “tag:” rather than the required `#tag` syntax. Round 2 client gives only general approval.
decisions.note: The presented tag-query interaction differs from the fixed reference, and bare approval does not qualify as explicit acceptance; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly lists “exact phrases.” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Quoted exact-phrase search conforms; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “AND/OR/NOT” and “(grouping)” but does not state whether operators must be quoted to become literal search terms. Round 2 client generally accepts without clarifying that rule.
decisions.note: Boolean operators and grouping are covered, but the mandatory literal-operator edge rule cannot be established from the presentation; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists newest, oldest, updated, title, and URL sorting. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Multiple sort keys conform; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerates “bulk read, favorite, archive, tag, delete,” but does not present the required unread action or both add-tag and remove-tag operations. Round 2 client gives only general approval.
decisions.note: The enumerated bulk-action set is narrower than the reference, and the response does not surface the difference; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly presents “select all N matching this filter,” not merely the current page. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Whole-filter bulk scope conforms; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents saving the “current query/view/sort”; the query language supports tag and NOT expressions. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: This is functionally equivalent to a reusable dynamic filter containing search and included/excluded tag conditions; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents Netscape HTML import and says folders map to tags, but does not state whether title, tags, and date-added are all preserved. Round 2 client generally accepts without clarifying preservation.
decisions.note: The format conforms, but the reference's required import-preservation semantics cannot be established from the presentation; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents export in “Netscape bookmark HTML (browser format).” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: The required export format is presented; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says snapshots save HTML locally and that “PDF pages [are] saved as-is.” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Local HTML preservation and the PDF-specific storage rule conform; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents one-click “Save to Internet Archive.” Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot creation conforms; implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents default view/sort, items per page, and text size preferences. Round 2 client accepts.
decisions.note: The requested display-related personal settings conform; implementation review.
